thread.title: European shares hit highest level in nearly two months, helped by tech rally By Reuters

author: Reuters
title: European shares hit highest level in nearly two months, helped by tech rally By Reuters
text:
© Reuters. European shares hit highest level in nearly two months, helped by tech rally LONDON, Jan 25 (Reuters) - European shares on Friday hit their highest level in nearly two months as investors flocked to technology stocks after positive U.S. earnings overnight, while news of slowing revenue growth from Vodafone VOD.L weighed on telecoms.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index .STOXX was up 0.6 percent by 0842 GMT, on track for its fourth straight weekly gain.
Frankfurt's DAX .GDAXI was the top performer, while Britain's exporter-heavy FTSE 100 .FTSE underperformed as a stronger sterling weighed.
The technology sector .SX8P hit its highest level since Nov. 11 as investors drew comfort from better-than-expected earnings overnight from U.S. chipmakers. They shrugged off a profit and sales warning and fourth-quarter sales miss from Intel INTC.O after the closing bell. .N
Xilinx Inc XLNX.O and Lam Research Corp LRCX.O reported quarterly results that beat analyst expectations, while Texas Instruments Inc TXN.O posted better-than-expected profits.
Those results helped soothe fears of stagnating smartphone demand and a cooling Chinese economy after sales warnings from Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Samsung (KS: 005930 ) and Taiwan Semiconductor earlier this month.
Car makers and parts suppliers .SXAP , which are sensitive to trade frictions and the health of the Chinese economy, were the strongest performers, hitting Dec. 3 highs. Mining and oil stocks also gained.
Telecoms .SXKP were the only sector in the red after disappointing results from Vodafone and Nordic telecom group Telia TELIA.ST .
Vodafone was down 1.2 percent, hitting its lowest in nearly nine years after the world's second-largest mobile operator said revenue growth slowed in the third quarter due to ongoing price competition in Spain and Italy and a slowdown in South Africa.
The stock was knocked hard on Thursday after its South African unit issued disappointing results.
Telia was down 4 percent, at the bottom of the STOXX 600 after its weaker-than-expected results, while Ericsson (BS: ERICAs ) rose 2.6 percent after the mobile telecoms equipment company beat fourth-quarter forecasts and highlighted thanks to growing demand for next-generation 5G gear.
The news will likely underscore expectations the Swedish company could be well placed to benefit from current turmoil surrounding market leader Huawei. and flavour maker Givaudan GIVN.S was not far behind, falling 3.5 percent after it said its weaker-than-expected net income in 2018 was hit by higher financing costs and foreign currency losses.
